title: Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE — Premium Revision Paper #17

pages.quiz:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #17
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. 'I saw a goat. ___ goat was brown.' Which article fits the blank? (1 mark)
   A. A
   B. An
   C. The
   D. Some

2. What is a signature? (1 mark)
   A. Your telephone number
   B. Your date of birth
   C. Your grade
   D. Your name written in your own handwriting

3. Which is written in block letters? (1 mark)
   A. WANJIKU KAMAU, in capital letters only
   B. wanjiku kamau, in small letters
   C. Wanjiku, in joined writing
   D. Wanjiku Kamau, with capitals at the start of each name

4. What should you do before you read a story? (1 mark)
   A. Read the last page only
   B. Write the answers
   C. Close the book
   D. Read the title and look at the pictures

5. Poems and similes: Which sentence has a simile? (1 mark)
   A. The runner was as fast as a cheetah.
   B. The runner was tired.
   C. The runner won the race.
   D. The race started at nine.

6. A sentence ends with (1 mark)
   A. a comma only
   B. a colon
   C. a capital letter
   D. a full stop, question mark or exclamation mark

7. What is a good way to find the meaning of an unknown word in a passage? (1 mark)
   A. Guess without reading
   B. Read the sentences around it for clues
   C. Ask a stranger
   D. Skip the passage

8. 'She sighed with relief' means she (1 mark)
   A. was very tired
   B. was afraid
   C. was very angry
   D. was happy that a worry was over

9. 'He is old enough to ride a bicycle.' Here enough comes (1 mark)
   A. before the verb
   B. at the end
   C. before the noun
   D. after the adjective

10. In the pattern 'enough + noun + to + verb', the word after 'to' is a (1 mark)
   A. verb
   B. adjective
   C. name
   D. noun

11. What should you do at a railway crossing? (1 mark)
   A. Stop, look and listen
   B. Play on the track
   C. Ride faster
   D. Run across

12. What does a foot bridge help people to do? (1 mark)
   A. Park cars
   B. Carry luggage
   C. Drive fast
   D. Cross a road safely by walking over it

13. Which foods help the body to grow? (1 mark)
   A. Beans, eggs, fish and meat
   B. Sugar and salt
   C. Air
   D. Tea only

14. Listening and diet: Which sentence is correct? (1 mark)
   A. I would like to being a nurse.
   B. I would likes to be a nurse.
   C. I would like be a nurse.
   D. I would like to be a nurse.

15. Which is an example of extensive reading? (1 mark)
   A. Reading many story books in your free time
   B. Learning a poem for an exam
   C. Reading one line for a test
   D. Writing a letter

16. The inbox is where (1 mark)
   A. the keyboard is stored
   B. messages waiting to be sent are kept
   C. messages you receive are kept
   D. deleted files are burnt

17. Dialogues: Which question is inferential? (1 mark)
   A. Which button did they click?
   B. Who wrote the address?
   C. Where do they see the reply?
   D. How do you think Baraka felt at the end?

18. What is a password? (1 mark)
   A. A type of email
   B. A secret word that only you know
   C. A public name
   D. A friend's address

19. Which is a polite offer? (1 mark)
   A. Would you like much tea bags?
   B. You would like a lot tea?
   C. Would you like many tea?
   D. Would you like some tea?

20. What must every sentence begin with? (1 mark)
   A. A full stop
   B. A question mark
   C. A capital letter
   D. A comma

21. Which is the best thing to do if an online message makes you afraid? (1 mark)
   A. Keep it a secret
   B. Reply to the stranger
   C. Send it to all your friends
   D. Show it to a trusted adult at once

22. Which is a good listening habit? (1 mark)
   A. Look out of the window
   B. Look at the speaker
   C. Shout answers before the question ends
   D. Talk to your neighbour

23. How do you make the question form of 'She is reading'? (1 mark)
   A. Is she reading?
   B. She is reading?
   C. Does she reading?
   D. Is reading she?

24. Which are pests? (1 mark)
   A. Sacks for storing maize
   B. Tall trees
   C. Tools for digging
   D. Small animals or insects that damage crops

25. Which is the correct negative of 'We planted beans'? (1 mark)
   A. We didn't plant beans.
   B. We not planted beans.
   C. We didn't planted beans.
   D. We don't planted beans.

26. Which is a simile? (1 mark)
   A. The goat was fast.
   B. The goat is a runner.
   C. The goat ran like the wind.
   D. The goat ran quickly.

27. How long should the narrative composition be at this level? (1 mark)
   A. About 60 to 80 words
   B. About 300 words
   C. About 10 words
   D. About 500 words

28. In which word does 'gh' say /f/? (1 mark)
   A. high
   B. laugh
   C. daughter
   D. night

29. In the story, why was Omondi standing alone? (1 mark)
   A. He had lost his shoes
   B. Other children refused to play with him because of his mother's illness
   C. He had a football
   D. He wanted to study

30. Which word in the story means 'said no to doing something'? (1 mark)
   A. nodded
   B. smiled
   C. noticed
   D. refused

31. Which word is an adverb of place? (1 mark)
   A. soon
   B. gently
   C. outside
   D. always

32. Which sentence uses the right word for how she sings? (1 mark)
   A. She sings good.
   B. She sings goodly.
   C. She sing well.
   D. She sings well.

33. What is the job of a comma? (1 mark)
   A. To show a question
   B. To show strong feeling
   C. To show a short pause and to separate items
   D. To end a sentence

34. What is a riddle? (1 mark)
   A. A list of rules
   B. A word puzzle that describes something without naming it
   C. A kind of song
   D. A long story

35. Which conjunction means the same as 'but' in 'The room was small, ____ it was very clean'? (1 mark)
   A. yet
   B. for
   C. nor
   D. so

36. In which tense is a description usually written? (1 mark)
   A. Future perfect
   B. Past perfect
   C. Command form
   D. Present tense

37. What is a digital text? (1 mark)
   A. A text printed on paper only
   B. A text read on a screen
   C. A hand-written letter
   D. A spoken poem

38. Which is a safe habit when searching online? (1 mark)
   A. Clicking every pop-up
   B. Using sites your teacher approves
   C. Sharing your address
   D. Telling strangers your password

39. Which is a good way to learn a hard spelling? (1 mark)
   A. Never write it
   B. Copy it wrongly
   C. Look, cover, write and check
   D. Guess it every time

40. In which person is a diary usually written? (1 mark)
   A. Third person (he, she)
   B. Second person (you)
   C. No person
   D. First person (I, we)

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Write two words in which 'gh' is silent and two in which it says /f/. (4 marks)

42. Write a narrative of about 60 words about a visit to a shop. Use one simile and two time words. (5 marks)

43. Write an SMS inviting a friend to your birthday party on Saturday at 3 o'clock. (3 marks)

44. Write a short dialogue of four lines in which you borrow a book from a friend politely. (4 marks)

45. Write three sentences about a car near a bridge using one subject pronoun, one object pronoun and one possessive pronoun. (3 marks)

46. Cross out the silent letter in each word: write, lamb, honest, listen. (2 marks)

47. Say whether the voice falls or rises at the end of: (a) Who sent the message? (b) Is the phone on the table? (2 marks)

48. Explain the difference between a factual and an inferential question and give an example of each from the story. (4 marks)

49. Write a polite request to borrow a ruler from a classmate. (2 marks)

50. Describe how to skim and how to scan a passage. (4 marks)

51. Make two sentences with 'very ... but ...' about shopping. (2 marks)

52. Write the plurals of: bus, story, wolf, mouse. (2 marks)

53. Give three questions to ask yourself when you proofread. (3 marks)

54. What lesson does the poem 'The Whistle' teach about winning and losing? (2 marks)

55. Explain how to use the five-finger test. (3 marks)

56. Write a question for each answer: (a) 'It is at the stadium.' (b) 'The coach.' (2 marks)

57. Write a short speech of four sentences about protecting a river. (4 marks)

58. List three details that a school library form may ask for. (3 marks)

59. Write one sentence using 'while' with the past progressive. (3 marks)

60. What kind of person is Baraka? Give one reason from the story. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #17 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — The
   The goat has already been mentioned, so we use the.

2. D — Your name written in your own handwriting
   A signature shows that you agree with what is written.

3. A — WANJIKU KAMAU, in capital letters only
   Block letters are capital letters.

4. D — Read the title and look at the pictures
   The title and pictures help you predict.

5. A — The runner was as fast as a cheetah.
   It compares the runner with a cheetah using as ... as.

6. D — a full stop, question mark or exclamation mark
   These are the marks that end sentences.

7. B — Read the sentences around it for clues
   Context clues help you understand new words.

8. D — was happy that a worry was over
   Relief is the feeling when a worry ends.

9. D — after the adjective
   With adjectives, enough comes after the adjective.

10. A — verb
   To is followed by a verb such as sit or eat.

11. A — Stop, look and listen
   Trains cannot stop quickly.

12. D — Cross a road safely by walking over it
   It goes over the road.

13. A — Beans, eggs, fish and meat
   They contain protein.

14. D — I would like to be a nurse.
   The pattern is would like to be + noun phrase.

15. A — Reading many story books in your free time
   Extensive reading means reading widely.

16. C — messages you receive are kept
   The outbox holds messages waiting to be sent.

17. D — How do you think Baraka felt at the end?
   You must work it out from clues.

18. B — A secret word that only you know
   A password protects your account.

19. D — Would you like some tea?
   We use some in offers.

20. C — A capital letter
   Capital letters start sentences.

21. D — Show it to a trusted adult at once
   A trusted adult can help you stay safe.

22. B — Look at the speaker
   Looking at the speaker shows you are listening.

23. A — Is she reading?
   Put is before the subject.

24. D — Small animals or insects that damage crops
   Pests eat or damage crops.

25. A — We didn't plant beans.
   After didn't, use the base form plant.

26. C — The goat ran like the wind.
   A simile compares using like or as.

27. A — About 60 to 80 words
   The task is a narrative of 60 to 80 words.

28. B — laugh
   'Gh' says /f/ in laugh, cough, enough and rough.

29. B — Other children refused to play with him because of his mother's illness
   The other children were afraid because they did not know the facts.

30. D — refused
   Some children refused to play with Omondi.

31. C — outside
   'Outside' tells where.

32. D — She sings well.
   'Well' is the adverb; 'good' is an adjective.

33. C — To show a short pause and to separate items
   Commas mark short pauses and separate list items.

34. B — A word puzzle that describes something without naming it
   The listener guesses the answer.

35. A — yet
   'Yet' shows a surprise, like 'but'.

36. D — Present tense
   Descriptions often say what something is like now.

37. B — A text read on a screen
   Digital texts are read on phones, tablets and computers.

38. B — Using sites your teacher approves
   Approved sites and private details keep you safe.

39. C — Look, cover, write and check
   Cover-write-check builds memory.

40. D — First person (I, we)
   A diary is about what I did and felt.

SECTION B
----
41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Silent: night, light, high, daughter (any two). /f/: laugh, cough, enough, rough (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word.

42. (5 marks)
   Answer: A story of about 60 words with beginning, middle and end, one simile, two time words such as first and then, and correct punctuation.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for beginning, events, simile, time words, and punctuation.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Hi Kamau. Please come to my birthday party on Saturday at 3 o'clock at my home. Thank you. Ann.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for greeting, 1 for day, time and place, 1 for politeness and name.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: A: Good morning, Ali. B: Good morning. A: May I borrow your book, please? B: Yes, here you are. A: Thank you.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for greeting, request, answer and thanks.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: It has bright head lights. The bridge protects us. The car is theirs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: write (w), lamb (b), honest (h), listen (t)
   Working / marking points: Half a mark for each.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: (a) falls (b) rises
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

48. (4 marks)
   Answer: A factual question has its answer stated in the text: 'Where was Omondi's mother?' An inferential question needs clues: 'How did Omondi feel at the start?'
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 for each example.

49. (2 marks)
   Answer: May I borrow your ruler, please?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for may I and 1 mark for please.

50. (4 marks)
   Answer: To skim, look at the title, pictures and the first sentence of each paragraph to get the main idea. To scan, look quickly for key words to find a particular fact.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for skimming and 2 marks for scanning.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example: The mango is very sweet, but it is small. The bag is very nice, but it is expensive.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sentence.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: buses, stories, wolves, mice
   Working / marking points: Half a mark for each.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: Does every sentence start with a capital letter? Are words spelt correctly? Does my story have a beginning, middle and end?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible question.

54. (2 marks)
   Answer: To be a good sport: lose without crying, shake hands with the other team and say 'Good try'.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the lesson and 1 for a reason from the poem.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: Open a page and read. Hold up a finger for each new word. Count the fingers: few means the book is right, many means it is too hard.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the method, 1 mark for few, 1 mark for many.

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: (a) Where is it? (b) Who is the man with the whistle?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each suitable question.

57. (4 marks)
   Answer: A greeting, two points such as not throwing rubbish in the river and planting trees on its bank, and a closing.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each element.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: Name, grade, date of birth, school name, address, class teacher, head teacher (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

59. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: Mother was cooking while I was doing my homework.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for while, 1 for was/were, 1 for verb-ing forms used correctly.

60. (3 marks)
   Answer: He is kind and brave. He went to talk to Omondi, explained the facts and invited him to play.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a quality and 2 for the evidence.
